body_ar:
الكلام صفة كمال لله سبحانه وتعالى، والله تعالى تكلم بكلمات تشريعية وكلمات كونية، وكما أنه تعالى يتكلم فهو أيضاً يتصف بالسكوت، ولكنه سكوت عن علم فهو صفة كمال لله تعالى.
كلمات الله الشرعية والكونية:
يقول الشيخ حفظه الله: [ويتكلم متى شاء بما شاء.................... ] التكلم صفة كمال لله عز وجل، وكلامه تعالى شرعي وكوني.......
ميزة الكلمات الشرعية:
والكلمات الشرعية لها ميزات: الميزة الأولى: هي الاختيار لها، فإن الله سبحانه وتعالى يصطفي لهذه الكلمات من شاء من خلقه، كما قال تعالى: اللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ حَيْثُ يَجْعَلُ رِسَالَتَهُ [الأنعام:124] ، في القراءة الأخرى: (اللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ حَيْثُ يَجْعَلُ رسالاته) وهنا بحث دقيق وهو في تفسير قوله: (رسالته) و(رسالاته) ما الفرق بينهما؟ والجواب: أن قوله (رسالته) هي الشريعة بكاملها، وقوله (رسالاته) هي الأحكام على كثرتها، فكل حكم رسالة بخصوصها، مثلما تكتب رسالة إلى شخص في أمر تريده ثم ترسل إليه رسالة أخرى، فكل ذلك يسمى رسالة وتجمع على رسائل، فكذلك نزول الملك بسورة أو بآيات يسمى رسالة، والشريعة بكاملها تسمى رسالة، فلهذا جمعت تارة وأفردت أخرى، وبهما قرئ في هذه الآية...
body_en:
*[Site synopsis]* Speech is an attribute of perfection for God, glorified and exalted is He. God, exalted is He, has spoken legislative words and cosmic words; and just as He, exalted is He, speaks, so He is also described by silence — but a silence that proceeds from knowledge, so that it too is an attribute of perfection for God, exalted is He.

## God's legislative and cosmic words

The Sheikh, may God preserve him, says:

*[And He speaks when He wills, with what He wills …………………]*

Speaking is an attribute of perfection for God, mighty and majestic, and His speech, exalted is He, is legislative and cosmic ……

## What distinguishes the legislative words

The legislative words have distinguishing features. The first is that they are chosen: God, glorified and exalted is He, selects for these words whom He wills of His creation, as He said, exalted is He: {God knows best where to place His message} (Sūrat al-Anʿām 6:124) — and in the other reading, {God knows best where to place His messages}.

Here there is a fine point of inquiry, in the interpretation of His words "His message" (risālatahu) and "His messages" (risālātihi): what is the difference between the two? The answer is that His words "His message" mean the revealed law in its entirety, while His words "His messages" mean the rulings in their multiplicity, for every ruling is a message in its own right — just as you write a letter to someone about a matter you want, then send him another letter, and all of that is called a letter, and the plural of it is letters. In the same way, the angel's descent with a chapter or with verses is called a message, and the revealed law in its entirety is called a message. It is for this reason that the word was made plural at one time and singular at another, and this verse has been read in both ways…

flags.note: The whole argument turns on one Arabic word carrying the revealed sense and the ordinary sense at once, which no single English word does. Splitting the rendering keeps the argument intelligible but costs the reader the identity of the term, so the Arabic is retained in brackets at the point of the distinction. A reviewer should decide whether a translator's note in the rendered page is preferable.

translator_notes: One of a run of fourteen records, IDs 734-747, the series 'The Names and Attributes', all built to the same template and all excerpts. Each carries a site-written synopsis, then a section heading, then the opening formula and the first lines of a lesson, and then breaks off on an ellipsis; the full text sits behind a .doc download in the /medias/doc/esmawesivat-* series, numbered 1 to 14 in the same order as the IDs.

The source's final line, 'تحميل المادة' ('download the material'), is the label of a download link in the page furniture, not part of the text. It is recorded as source_download_link and omitted from body_ar and body_en.

This record does carry a CMS timestamp in a .create_date span (10 May 2011, within a 28-minute window shared by the whole run 738-747). That is a bulk-upload timestamp for the series, not the date the lesson was given, and it is not evidence of composition date. Record 737, translated in an earlier wave, reports no date for this run; the timestamp is in fact present in the page and should be backfilled there.
Qur'anic renderings here are interpretive and are not a substitute for the Arabic.
Creedal material. Per style guide section 8, the vocabulary of divine attributes is not the vocabulary of the five legal rulings and the five-rulings mapping is not applied anywhere in this record.

The synopsis announces the divine attribute of silence, and the record breaks off long before reaching it; the first of several 'distinguishing features' is the last thing on the page. Marked critical_for_display.

Two separate rows of dots inside the quoted verse and after 'legislative and cosmic' are the source's own elisions, not the translator's. They are kept in both panes so the reader can see where the source itself cut the text.
